title: High School Teacher Arrested for Clapping in Support of Anti-Data Center Activists
excerpt: A local high school physics teacher was hauled out by four police officers for clapping six times during a city commission meeting.
content_html:
Sign up to see the future, today

Can’t-miss innovations from the bleeding edge of science and tech

If you’re among the millions of US citizens against power-hungry data centers going up in your town, you may want to be careful about how you exercise your First Amendment right to protest.

Last week, high school physics teacher Lux Claridge was hauled out of a public meeting by four police officers for the baffling crime of clapping in support of an anti-data center speaker. During the public comment portion of the meeting, held by the Emporia City Commission in Lyon County, Kansas, residents who showed up to voice opposition to a 1,000-acre data center project were warned against “clapping” and “snapping” in support of speakers.

“It was very clear at the beginning that each person is given their two minutes, and we’re trying to be respectful of that,” Emporia commissioner Monica Duncan warned those in attendance, footage of the meeting shared on social media shows. “Snapping, clapping, any other rude comments or anything — we will ask you to leave.”

As one speaker later wrapped up her two-minute comment period, stating “we are the people, and the table belongs to us,” Claridge was filmed clapping his hands together a total of six times.

“Chief, will you take the next person out that claps or anything?” an unidentified commissioner, likely Duncan, then asked Emporia police chief Ed Owens.

At the commissioners’ request, four police officers then swarmed Claridge, who challenged them to “drag me out,” which they did after placing the physics teacher in handcuffs.

Speaking to local channel KWCH after their arrest, an undeterred Claridge said they are “glad to be out,” but that it was just an “inconvenience, really.”

“It’s not really deterring me from speaking out or I guess, clapping,” Claridge continued.

Other attendees were understandably shaken after witnessing the brazen escalation against a citizen expressing themselves at a public hearing. Interviewed by KWCH, Claridge’s brother David said he’s “looking at avenues to get these people recalled,” calling the level of force used “insane.”

“We are citizens of this community; we have a right to do our constitutionally protected activities, which is exactly what they’re violating at this time,” another anonymous local told the outlet. “I think we’re all in a state of fear because of what this government’s doing to us.”

The data center in question, known as the “Flint Hills Digital Campus,” is a planned hyperscale data center. If it ever gets built, could easily be the largest data center in the state of Kansas.

The hypocrisy on display at the meeting where Claridge was arrested — where procedural rules are clearly being weaponized against concerned citizens — may be particularly acute in the small Kansas town, but it’s also part and parcel of the situation unfolding all across the United States as distrust with the tech industry soars to unprecedented heights.

When big business interests march into town, civic leaders and their watchdogs on the local police force roll out the red carpet — Emporia commissioners voted unanimously to annex over 1,000 acres for Pinkston’s data center just one day after it was announced — yet when the people who live there ask to be included in the process, they’re insulted by officials, surveilled by police, and hauled off to jail.

Data centers aren’t new in that regard, but they do reflect the growing imposition of moneyed tech interests into the everyday lives of common people. As Emporia journalist Max McCoy wrote: “The system is built to reward money and influence, and nothing is likely to change as long as wealth is prized over humanity. But every so often we get a glimpse behind the curtain, and we are rightly appalled.”

content_html_zh:
今天就注册以了解未来

不容错过的前沿科技创新

如果您是反对在您所在城镇建立耗电数据中心的数百万美国公民之一，那么您可能需要谨慎行使第一修正案的抗议权。

上周，高中物理教师勒克斯·克拉里奇 (Lux Claridge) 因鼓掌支持反数据中心发言人的莫名其妙的罪行，被四名警察从一次公开会议中带走。 在堪萨斯州里昂县恩波里亚市委员会举行的会议的公众评论部分，对 1,000 英亩数据中心项目表示反对的居民被警告不要“鼓掌”和“厉声”支持发言者。

社交媒体上分享的会议视频显示，恩波里亚专员莫妮卡邓肯警告与会者：“一开始就很清楚，每个人都有两分钟的发言时间，我们正在努力尊重这一点。” “拍手、鼓掌、任何其他粗鲁的评论或任何其他行为——我们都会请你离开。”

当一位发言者后来结束她两分钟的评论时说“我们是人民，桌子属于我们”时，克拉里奇总共拍了六次双手。

“队长，你能把下一个鼓掌的人带出去吗？” 随后，一位身份不明的专员（可能是邓肯）询问恩波里亚警察局长埃德·欧文斯。

应委员们的要求，四名警察随后涌向克拉里奇，克拉里奇要求他们“把我拖出去”，他们在给物理老师戴上手铐后照做了。

克拉里奇在被捕后接受当地 KWCH 频道采访时表示，他们“很高兴能出去”，但这只是“真的带来不便”。

“这并没有真正阻止我发言，或者我猜是鼓掌，”克拉里奇继续说道。

其他与会者在目睹针对一名在公开听证会上表达自己意见的公民的公然升级后，感到震惊，这是可以理解的。 克拉里奇的弟弟大卫在接受 KWCH 采访时表示，他正在“寻找召回这些人的途径”，并称使用武力的程度“疯狂”。

另一位不愿透露姓名的当地人告诉媒体：“我们是这个社区的公民；我们有权进行受宪法保护的活动，而这正是他们此时所违反的。” “我认为，由于这个政府对我们所做的事情，我们都处于恐惧之中。”

该数据中心被称为“弗林特山数字园区”，是一个规划中的超大规模数据中心。 如果它建成的话，很可能成为堪萨斯州最大的数据中心。

克拉里奇被捕的会议上所表现出的虚伪——程序规则显然被用来对付相关公民——在这个堪萨斯小镇可能尤其严重，但随着对科技行业的不信任飙升到前所未有的高度，这也是整个美国局势的重要组成部分。

当大型商业利益集团进军城镇时，当地警察部队的公民领袖和他们的监督者会铺上红地毯——恩波里亚委员们一致投票决定吞并平克斯顿数据中心的 1,000 多英亩土地，仅在宣布这一消息一天后——然而，当住在那里的人们要求参与这一过程时，他们却遭到了官员的侮辱，受到警察的监视，并被投入监狱。

数据中心在这方面并不新鲜，但它们确实反映出金钱技术利益越来越多地融入普通人的日常生活。 正如恩波里亚记者马克斯·麦考伊（Max McCoy）所写：“这个体系的建立是为了奖励金钱和影响力，只要财富优先于人性，什么都不会改变。 但时不时地，我们会瞥见幕后的一幕，我们理所当然地感到震惊。”
